claims.text: Chemical short-range order typically suppresses lattice thermal conductivity in concentrated refractory high-entropy alloys relative to a fully disordered solid solution.
SRO enhances phonon scattering by breaking translational symmetry.
Ordered clusters introduce mass and strain-field fluctuations that enhance phonon scattering.
MoNbTaW is a body-centered-cubic refractory high-entropy alloy.
WTaMoNbV can serve as a body-centered-cubic concentrated refractory high-entropy alloy for this hypothesis.
MoNbTaW can possess a significant energetic driving force for chemical short-range ordering.
High-temperature annealing followed by rapid quenching can produce and retain a random atomic distribution in the stated RHEAs.
SRO is thermodynamically favored and kinetically accessible in the stated RHEAs between approximately 600 K and 1200 K.
Controlled thermal aging at an ordering temperature induces SRO in the alloy.
SRO clusters in these RHEAs feature preferential nearest-neighbor bonds such as Mo-Nb or Ta-W pairs.
Preferential local bonding produces local variations in atomic mass and interatomic force constants.
Lattice thermal conductivity is inversely related to the phonon scattering rate.
Phonon scattering in a disordered solid solution is dominated by point-defect mass variance and strain fields.
SRO regions act as superlattice-like defects that scatter phonons whose wavelengths are comparable to the SRO correlation length.
The additional scattering caused by SRO reduces phonon mean free path and therefore suppresses lattice thermal conductivity.
SRO hinders dislocation motion in MoNbTaW.
SRO-ordered samples will have 10-25% lower lattice thermal conductivity than disordered samples of identical composition.
The conductivity suppression will be greatest at intermediate temperatures and diminish at high temperatures because Umklapp scattering dominates.
Long-range ordered precipitates would cause a potentially more severe conductivity reduction through grain-boundary and phase-interface scattering.
The SRO effect on lattice thermal conductivity should be strongest in alloys with high atomic-mass variance and strong ordering enthalpies.
